neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert. Quiet, reduced spontaneous speech. MoCA 23/30: executive tasks impaired (trails 0/1, 6 F-words in 1 minute — impaired), memory (2/5 delayed recall), naming 2/3. PHQ-9: 12 (moderate depression — 'persistent sadness and lack of motivation'). IMPORTANT CLINICAL NOTE: The examiner asks her to describe her work as a chaplain — she recounts a single anecdote from 20 years ago, repeated verbatim twice in 10 minutes. When asked about her daughter, she makes an empathy-incongruent statement ('she worries too much') without the warmth expected from the relationship history the daughter described.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal strength 5/5. Normal tone. No tremor, no rigidity.
neurological_exam.additional: DIAGNOSTIC PUZZLE: (1) PHQ-9 12 — moderate depression symptoms; (2) Widowhood 3 years ago — major grief precipitant; (3) Prior MDD history; (4) Methotrexate — can rarely cause neurotoxicity (folate antagonism); (5) Hydroxychloroquine — very rarely CNS effects; (6) The VERBATIM STORY REPETITION and empathy-incongruent response noted during exam are behavioral FTD signs that are easily missed as 'depression' — but depressed patients do not repeat the exact same anecdote verbatim twice in one visit without noticing. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: depression causes psychomotor slowing, negative cognition, and tearfulness — FTD causes perseveration and social cognition loss. These can superficially overlap but are qualitatively different.

patient.chief_complaint: Worsening depression, personality change, and resignation from chaplain position — 22 months; referred by psychiatrist for 'treatment-resistant depression with atypical features'
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. H is a 58-year-old hospital chaplain — recently resigned as director of pastoral care — with a history of recurrent major depressive disorder and rheumatoid arthritis, referred by her psychiatrist for 'treatment-resistant depression with atypical features.' Her adult daughter is the primary historian. Ms. H became widowed 3 years ago when her husband died of a sudden cardiac event, and her daughter initially attributed the changes to complicated grief. Over the past 22 months, however, the changes have progressed in ways that have seemed increasingly non-grief-related to her daughter. She resigned her position as director of pastoral care 6 months ago after a series of incidents that were completely out of character. Colleagues reported that she had begun delivering the same prayer verbatim at every bedside visit, regardless of the patient's religious tradition or the circumstances of the visit. She repeatedly sent the same email to staff members — sometimes 6-8 times — each time appearing unaware she had sent it before. She made several inappropriate comments to grieving families — including laughing at a child's drawing in a way that distressed the family. The hospital chaplaincy director described her as 'completely different from the compassionate and perceptive person she had been for 22 years.' At home, she has developed an extraordinary rigidity around mealtimes and daily sequences. She arranges her medications in the same specific order every morning, becoming highly distressed if this routine is disrupted. She has stopped calling her grandchildren, whom she previously called every Sunday without fail. Her PHQ-9 is 12 — reporting sadness and lack of motivation. However, her psychiatrist notes that antidepressant adjustments and two cognitive behavioral therapy courses have not changed the trajectory. The diagnostic challenge: depression is real and present, with a clear precipitant (widowhood) and prior history. But depression does not cause verbatim story repetition, loss of social empathy, and perseverative email sending. Methotrexate neurotoxicity is rare but should be considered. The combination of MDD + grief + methotrexate creates a situation where FTD behavioral signs are easily misattributed to psychiatric disease.

output.test_type: Neuropsychological battery with depression-FTD differentiation focus

findings.finding: PHQ-9: 12 (moderate depression). GDS: 8/15 (mild-moderate depression on geriatric scale). Both scales confirm depressive symptoms.

HOWEVER — behavioral severity measures: FBI (Frontal Behavioral Inventory, informant-rated): 32/72 (markedly elevated — severe behavioral symptoms). NPI (Neuropsychiatric Inventory): total score 28 — elevated for disinhibition (7), apathy (8), and repetitive behaviors (8).
Executive function (DKEFS): Severely impaired — Trails condition 4: 4th percentile. Color-word inhibition: 5th percentile. These scores are far below what depression alone would produce.
Social cognition (Eyes test): 16/36 (<5th percentile). Faux Pas: 2/10 (<2nd percentile). Depression does NOT cause this pattern of severe social cognition impairment.
Episodic memory: HVLT-R delayed recall: 3/12 (10th percentile). Recognition 8/12 (30th percentile) — better than free recall.

output.impression: Marked executive dysfunction (DKEFS Trails condition 4: 4th percentile; Color-Word Inhibition: 5th percentile) and severely impaired social cognition (Reading the Mind in the Eyes: 16/36, <5th percentile; Faux Pas: 2/10, <2nd percentile) with moderate episodic memory impairment. Behavioral rating scales are markedly elevated (FBI 32/72; NPI total 28). The degree of executive and social cognition impairment is consistent with probable behavioral-variant FTD. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia — MAPT P301L pathogenic variant — tauopathy — with concurrent major depressive disorder (comorbid, not causal)

differential.key_features: Depression (PHQ-9 12) is present but does NOT explain verbatim perseveration, severely impaired social cognition, frontal FDG-PET hypometabolism, or MRI frontal atrophy; depression does not cause frontal neurodegeneration; MAPT genetic confirmation establishes bvFTD as primary
Grief can trigger FTD onset or worsen symptoms, but 22-month progressive syndrome with structural neuroimaging changes and genetic confirmation cannot be attributed to grief
No white matter lesions on MRI (methotrexate neurotoxicity causes FLAIR white matter changes); normal methotrexate level; normal folate and homocysteine
Amyloid PET negative; no posterior cingulate sign; frontal FDG-PET predominance; MAPT mutation confirmed (MAPT tauopathy is distinct from AD tauopathy)

critical_actions: The KEY discriminating test: depression does NOT cause severe social cognition impairment (Reading the Mind in the Eyes, Faux Pas) — this finding is pathognomonic for bvFTD when present in the context of behavioral syndrome
FDG-PET is essential to distinguish depression-related mild frontal changes from primary FTD frontotemporal hypometabolism
Methotrexate neurotoxicity must be actively excluded — though clinically unlikely, it is a treatable cause and requires workup
contraindicated_actions: Increasing antidepressants without FTD workup when behavioral syndrome has atypical features for depression
key_reasoning_points: DEPRESSION vs bvFTD discriminating features: (1) depression causes psychomotor slowing, tearfulness, negative cognition — NOT perseveration; (2) depression does NOT cause severe social cognition impairment; (3) FDG-PET in depression may show mild bilateral frontal/prefrontal reduction but NOT the severe frontotemporal pattern with posterior preservation seen in FTD

Methotrexate neurotoxicity requires specific MRI assessment: periventricular FLAIR white matter changes are the signature — when MRI white matter is normal and methotrexate level is therapeutic, neurotoxicity is effectively excluded

MAPT tauopathy produces tau-PET-positive, amyloid-PET-negative pattern — this distinguishes MAPT-FTD from Alzheimer's disease (which is both tau-positive and amyloid-positive) and from TDP-43 pathology (which is tau-PET negative)
Verbatim story repetition (the same anecdote word for word, twice in one visit, unaware of repetition) is a clinical sign of perseverative FTD behavior — this is NOT a feature of depression or grief

red_herrings.intended_effect: Consider rheumatoid arthritis-related CNS vasculitis or neurological complication
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: RA neurological complications (pachymeningitis, vasculitis) are rare and require CSF/MRI features that are absent; normal ESR and CRP indicate well-controlled RA; anti-CCP and RF are not relevant to the FTD workup

red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute entire behavioral syndrome to treatment-resistant major depression and complicated grief
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Depression and grief can coexist with bvFTD; the verbatim perseveration, severely impaired social cognition, and frontotemporal neuroimaging changes cannot be explained by depression alone — MAPT genetic confirmation establishes FTD as primary

metadata.notes: Diagnostic puzzle bvFTD — MAPT P301L mutation masquerading as treatment-resistant depression. Key teaching: social cognition testing (Eyes test, Faux Pas) discriminates FTD from depression; methotrexate neurotoxicity requires MRI white matter assessment; MAPT tauopathy is tau-PET positive, amyloid-PET negative.
